title: Refactor affordance log — small API surface & quick wins
content:
Context: quick personal scratch for small-scope refactors I keep bumping into during PR reviews. Goal: produce tiny, low-risk changes that (a) reduce cognitive load, (b) make future refactors easier, and (c) have a clear backout plan. Keep this minimal so I can paste into PR descriptions or create tiny follow-up tickets.

Why this doc: too many review threads spiral into big rewrites; instead collect small affordances (API ergonomics, naming, micro-abstractions) to apply post-merge or in a separate small PR. Use these heuristics when deciding whether to comment or leave for a follow-up.

Decision heuristics (quick):
- If change touches public SDK/API surface -> escalate to short RFC or coordinate with SDK owners. Not a tiny PR.
- If change is purely internal helper rename / local extraction with < 8 LOC change in call sites -> do inline tiny follow-up.
- If test coverage required for behavioral change -> block on test or move to follow-up with explicit test plan.
- Prefer adding small adapters over churn in call sites (adapter pattern for compatibility).

Recent entries (log):
- 2026-01-05: Extracted kv_cache_key_builder from runtime/router to serving/kv/utils. Rationale: multiple call-sites building composite keys in slightly different ways. Outcome: reduced duplication, easier to add telemetry for collisions.
  - Follow-up: add microbenchmark for key build latency (ENGINF-1245)

- 2026-02-10: Short-circuited health-check path for dedicated mode. Added minimal wrapper so route handler doesn't see DedicatedConfig. Rationale: protect handler surface from config objects.
  - Rollback plan: revert wrapper function (one file), tests cover happy path.

Checklist for a tiny follow-up PR (use as template in body):
- PR title: "small: extract <thing> from <file> (affordance)"
- One-line rationale + risk (why small)
- Files changed: list (expected small)
- Tests added/updated: yes/no + brief description (unit/fixture)
- Performance/regression risk: negligible / microbenchmark attached / see ENGINF-####
- Backout: single revert commit targeted at extract
- Linked issues: ENGINF-#### or GH PRs

Common affordances to look for (my checklist while scanning a PR):
- Repeated inline composition of strings/keys -> candidate for util extractor
- 3+ conditionals around same flag -> small config accessor helper
- Similar try/catch blocks duplicated -> small helper to normalize error handling
- Repeated creation of context objects with same defaults -> factory function
- Public route handlers using internal-only classes -> create adapter to limit surface

Naming & API guidance (short):
- Prefer explicit "forX" functions instead of overloaded booleans (e.g., buildKeyForShard(v) > buildKey(v, true))
- Avoid global config reads in helpers; inject narrow interface instead (only methods needed)
- Keep adapter functions in same package as callers to avoid circular deps

Mini refactor patterns (code sketch style)
- Extractor pattern:
  // before: repeated in 4 files
  prefix := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", model, tenant)
  key := fmt.Sprintf("%s:cache:%d", prefix, version)

  // after:
  func BuildCacheKey(model, tenant string, version int) string {
    return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s:cache:%d", model, tenant, version)
  }

- Adapter pattern for handlers:
  // create thin interface with only `Serve(context.Context, Input) (Output, error)`
  // implement adapter that converts internal types -> handler input

Backout & testing notes (short):
- Always include a smoke test that hits the unchanged external route (happy path). If the change is internal-only, add a unit test for the extractor/adapter.
- If adding telemetry spans, wrap in feature flag so we can disable without code revert.

Follow-ups / TODOs (to convert into tickets):
- [ ] ENGINF-1299: Add microbenchmark for kv key builder latency (assign Liam)
- [ ] ENGINF-1302: Create SDK-compatible adapter for route /v1/stream -> reduces duplication in hosted API handlers (spike + small PR)
- [ ] ENGINF-1310: Audit public handlers for dependency on internal config objects (low effort: grep + list)

PR templates / copy-paste snippets (for quick use):
- Rationale snippet: "Small refactor: extracted <function> to remove duplication across handlers. No behavior change. See tiny tests in <file> and linked microbenchmark. Backout: revert commit <sha>."

Notes to self (open questions):
- How much do we tolerate helper proliferation? Need a brief guideline: 1 helper per 3 duplicates? (agree with Noelle?)
- When is an adapter actually worth it vs a one-off single use? threshold: 2+ call sites and at least one planned future use.

Links / search hints for later:
- Search terms: "cache key", "BuildCacheKey", "kv cache", "adapter", "wrapDedicatedConfig"
- Useful PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/9876 (kv key extract), https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/10421 (health-wrapper)

Quick mental model for reviewers:
- If your comment would force 10+ files to change, prefer filing a follow-up ticket and make a minimal in-review patch that documents the plan.
- Small PRs win: they're easier to test, revert, and reason about. Prefer this when safety is primary.

End — drop into PR descriptions or convert to a follow-up ticket when I have >1 affordance collected per area.

Notes-to-self tags: #affordance #tiny-pr #postmerge
